profile: SQLite 3.47.2 UTF-8 with the scalar envelope defined by sqlite-scalars-v1.json and IEEE binary64.
scope: The division, remainder, bitwise AND and OR, and signed shifts of two checked scalar operands in their written order.
admission: Every closed scalar operand already admitted in an arithmetic role. The owning scope applies the existing bounds, reference validation and parameter-registration rules.
meaning: Propagate NULL for each operator when either operand is NULL.

Division uses truncated signed integer division for two integer numeric operands. A zero divisor returns NULL. Use a binary64 quotient when either numeric operand is REAL or MIN divided by minus one overflows.

Remainder uses INTEGER conversion of both operands and truncation toward zero to determine the integer remainder. A zero converted divisor returns NULL. The remainder is returned with REAL storage if either operand is treated as REAL under arithmetic numeric coercion.

Bitwise operators apply INTEGER conversion and 64-bit two's-complement operations. A negative shift distance reverses direction. A right shift preserves the sign bit. A shift of at least 64 positions yields the value determined by the direction and sign.
Arithmetic coercion distinguishes stored numbers, embedded decimal prefixes in TEXT and BLOB, and the numeric result of each nested operand.
sql: Emit the explicit binary operator inside the existing paired parentheses, preserving both sides and their association at every depth.
observations: Exact INTEGER and REAL storage, signed zero, finite and infinite REAL results, NULLs, column identities and names, and numbered binding registration.

finite.identity: Read root, operator and both operand IDs from the returned IR and exhaust the 2 × 6 × 12² Cartesian product.

exploration.structure: Generate nested numeric trees in both root families. Change operand types, shift boundaries, aliases, repeated bindings and negative divisors. Cover every operator through constructed structures.
